title: Git-folder sync S2.2: restore tasks a resolved folder adds to an enrolled destination, with named refusals
outcome: Git-folder sync S2.2: restore tasks a resolved folder adds to an enrolled destination, with named refusals
acceptance: On an enrolled destination, each task the resolved folder adds is restored in the folder's single transaction exactly as the empty-graph import restores one: its incoming id; a generation-zero restored record and an import origin whose snapshot comes from the whole resolved tree (root id, short ref); its prerequisites and blockers, and when the profile shares them its notes as inert restored history and its activity in the origin; no work event and no run, claim, root execution or expected contributor; a Completed addition keeps its reported completion without a seal. Admitted scalar edits in the same folder apply together. Added tasks join the exchange baseline and export exactly as the folder carries them; exact replay and dry run behave as for edits. A destination that holds an exchange baseline always takes this delta admission, even when its current export is empty; only an unenrolled store bootstraps.

Adds and edits are admitted together before any write. A refused add refuses the whole folder, writes nothing, and the bounded task-id-ordered message names each refused task with one reason: id_collision (a work id held anywhere in the store including a task the exchange retired, a short ref held in this project, a blocker id held in the store including a cleared one, a shared note id held by an import origin or a local object, or an activity (origin_machine, activity_id) already held); unsupported_origin (a parent, prerequisite or superseded_by reference to a task held here without a task-sync import origin); origin_graph (the prospective union of every existing import-origin document plus the additions fails closure, cycle, hierarchy-limit, notice-identity or computed-root validation, attributed to the additions involved); ancestor_binding (any held or added ancestor in the prospective chain cannot take unfinished work: a held ancestor fails the scalar edit admission, a Completed ancestor would gain an unfinished added task, or the affected root has an active root execution, named by its id); and record-id pins in acceptance bindings refuse in preflight, never during insertion.

Existing tasks' notes and activity are compared exactly by the planner, so an unchanged native note never blocks an add and a change is unsupported_fields; added tasks' notices are collision-checked per task; a note or activity added locally since the basis refuses through the export-basis check. The new baseline is recorded inside the transaction before the final export check; the final foreign-key check and origin audit remain rollback guards, and a failure there is a projection bug, never a silent drop.

Doctor (verify_all) is healthy after adds, including the cross-origin graph audit; repair rebuilds only disposable projections and preserves all durable rows; fail-first tests cover the cases above, including the two-host CLI return leg with notes and activity enabled (host A's native task passes through unchanged on its way back, a new task from B is restored, a later edit of the native task on A refuses).

completion.summary: S2.2 landed as 8019563df8ee1001f3e622f6b69dbfd84214db07 on origin/master: an enrolled destination restores the tasks a resolved folder adds, in the folder's single transaction exactly as the empty-graph import restores them, beside admitted scalar edits. A refused addition refuses the whole folder with bounded, task-id-ordered reasons: id_collision (activity and note ids alias-free), acceptance_pin, unsupported_origin, ancestor_binding, refused_reference, retained_graph and origin_graph. Graph attribution follows the validator's order, finds cycles as strongly connected components and sets dependents aside. The final FK check and origin audit raise InvalidWorkProjection.
